newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shangri-La 1996 occupancy, room rates up.
newsitem.headline: Shangri-La 1996 occupancy, room rates up.

text.p: Hotel owner Shangri-La Asia Ltd said on Friday increased contributions from the group's Hong Kong, Philippine and Fiji hotels helped lift the company's 1996 net profit by 27 percent to HK$1.09 billion.
"The group's two hotels (in Hong Kong) benefited from strong arrivals in 1996 which increased by 14.7 percent over 1995," the company said in a statement accompanying its 1996 results.

This contributed to overall occupancy of 88 percent in 1996 versus 85 percent in 1995 at its hotels in Kowloon and on Hong Kong island. The average room rate increased by six percent at the Kowloon Shangri-La to HK$1,750 and by eight percent at the Island Shangri-La to HK$2,131, it added.

The company, which benefited from an improving Philippine economy, said business was stronger at its Manila hotels -- with the Shangri-La Hotel's occupancy rate up four percent and its room rate up 13 percent, and the Edsa Plaza Hotel's occupancy rate up seven percent and its room rate up three percent.

Occupancy in its Mactan Island Resort in Cebu was steady at 79 percent, affected by a room extension programme to be completed in mid-1997, the company said. The room rate rose by three percent in 1996, it said.
"Both hotels in Fiji saw occupancies recovering from 56 percent to 68 percent at the Fijian Resort and from 67 to 80 percent for the Fiji Mocambo Hotel," the company said.
Combined average room rates in the Fijian hotels rose by 16 percent last year.
Occupancy at its Jakarta hotel rose by 15 percent to 75 percent in 1996, helped by increased foreign arrivals to the Indonesian capital, but the average room rate fell by three percent to HK$1,040.

Shangri-La's China hotels posted a mixed year, with the combined average occupancy achieved by its seven hotels staying at the same level as the previous year at 69 percent. Combined average room rate eased to HK$899 from HK$920 in 1995.

The company said total rental revenue at its 50 percent owned China World Trade Central (CWTC) in Beijing increased by 17 percent to HK$779 million and its Shanghai Centre added 16 percent to HK$467 million.
The CWTC has obtained approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) for an overseas listing to finance the expansion of its business, it said.
"The company will make an announcement when the new structure of CWTC is finalised by CWTC's board of directors and after CSRC has given its final approval," it added.
Shangri-La said it looked forward to further growth with the continued economic advancement of the Asia Pacific region.

"The group's hotels in Hong Kong, Philippines, Jarkata and Fiji should benefit from stronger demand in 1997 and the three hotels which opened in China during 1996 are expected to raise market share in their respective cities," Shangri-La said.
"While the immediate outlook for the group's hotels in Beijing, Hangzhou and Shenzhen is mixed, they stand to benefit when market conditions improve," it added.

The company also said it agreed with its partner China National Metals and Minerals Import and Export Corp to extend the joint venture period for Beijing Shangri-La Hotel Ltd by 30 years to 2035, and to expand the hotel facilities.
Shangri-La said it would cut its interest in the Beijing venture in favour of the Chinese partner from the current 49 percent to 43.5 percent in 1998 and to 38 percent in 1999.
